items.question: What connects A.P. Hill, George McClellan, and Ellen Marcy?
items.answer: Love triangle. A.P. Hill and George McClellan both courted Ellen Marcy, who chose McClellan. This poisoned Hill's relationship with his former roommate.

items.question: What connects Grant, Longstreet, and the Republican Party?
items.answer: Post-war politics. Longstreet became a Republican — Grant's party — after the Civil War, destroying his reputation in the South. Grant rewarded his loyalty with federal appointments.

items.question: What connects the Class of 1842, the Class of 1843, and the Class of 1846?
items.answer: They produced the war's key commanders. Class of 1842: Longstreet, D.H. Hill, Rosecrans, Pope. Class of 1843: Grant. Class of 1846: Jackson, McClellan, Pickett, and 22 generals total.

items.question: What connects D.H. Hill, Stonewall Jackson, and college presidencies?
items.answer: Marriage and academia. D.H. Hill married Jackson's sister Isabella. After the war, Hill became a college president; Jackson was a VMI professor before the war.

items.question: What connects the Mexican-American War and Appomattox?
items.answer: Training ground. Nearly every major Civil War general served together in the Mexican-American War (1846-1848), forming relationships that played out at Appomattox 17 years later.
items.stem: What connects the Mexican-American War and Appomattox?
items.correct: Training ground. Nearly every major Civil War general served together in the Mexican-American War (1846-1848), forming relationships that played out at Appomattox 17 years later.

items.question: What connects Lewis Armistead, Winfield Scott Hancock, and Gettysburg?
items.answer: Enemies at Gettysburg. Armistead and Hancock were best friends before the war. At Gettysburg, Armistead led a Confederate brigade in Pickett's Charge against Hancock's Union position. Both were wounded; Armistead died asking for Hancock.

items.question: What connects Beauregard, Robert Anderson, and Fort Sumter?
items.answer: Student vs. teacher. Beauregard had been an artillery student of Major Robert Anderson at West Point. When Beauregard bombarded Fort Sumter, Anderson was the Union commander inside. The first shot was a West Pointer firing on his own instructor.

items.question: This West Point class produced 22 generals from 59 graduates — a 37% general rate unmatched in Academy history. Name the class and at least 3 of its members.
items.answer: Class of 1846. Members include: Stonewall Jackson, George B. McClellan, George Pickett, A.P. Hill, John Sedgwick, Samuel Sturgis, Cadmus Wilcox.
